Anemia is a condition characterized by a deficiency in the number or quality of red blood cells, which leads to reduced oxygen transport throughout the body.

Asphyxiation may occur as a result of exclusion of oxygen from the air by physiologically relatively inert gases or by interference with oxygen transport within the body by inhalation of metabolic poisons
The gas poisons intracellular oxygen transport mechanisms and manifests effects particularly on heart and liver.
Iron: required for oxygen transport (haemoglobin) and collagen hydroxylation; deficiency causes tissue hypoxia and impaired healing
Function: Oxygen transport (hemoglobin, myoglobin), electron transport, DNA synthesis
